subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the additive inverse of the matrix with rows (i, 0, 1), (0, −i, 2) and (−1, 1, 5).

mark_split.label: State what the additive inverse is
Change the sign of every entry

recall_prompt: Say what the additive inverse of a matrix is and how you would write it here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State what the additive inverse is
steps.margin_note: First mark. The additive inverse of A is the matrix −A for which A + (−A) = O, the zero matrix of the same order. Naming that property is the first mark.
steps.memory_tip: Additive inverse means the matrix that adds to zero, so it is A with every sign changed.
lines: The additive inverse of A is the matrix
−A for which A + (−A) = O, the zero
So −A is A with every sign changed.

recall.must_convey: That the additive inverse is the matrix −A satisfying A + (−A) = O, which means every entry changes sign.
accept: the additive inverse is minus A, the matrix that adds to the zero matrix
it is the matrix you add to A to get all zeros
A plus its additive inverse is the zero matrix, so change every sign

negate every entry so the sum is the null matrix

steps.why: The additive inverse is defined by the property A + (−A) = O, not by a formula. The rule 'change every sign' follows from that property, because addition acts on each position separately.
common_mistakes: Confusing the additive inverse −A with the multiplicative inverse A⁻¹.
Writing the zero matrix O as the answer instead of −A.

steps.label: Change the sign of every entry
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Every entry changes sign, the complex ones included: i becomes −i, and −i becomes i. Entries that are 0 stay 0.
steps.memory_tip: The sign flips for complex entries too: i becomes −i and −i becomes i. Zero stays zero.
lines: Change the sign of every entry:

recall.must_convey: That every entry is negated, giving rows (−i, 0, −1), (0, i, −2) and (1, −1, −5).
accept: negate each entry so i becomes minus i and minus i becomes i
the answer has rows minus i zero minus one, zero i minus two, one minus one minus five

steps.why: Matrix addition is defined position by position, so the sum is the zero matrix exactly when each entry cancels its partner. That forces −A to be A with each entry negated.
common_mistakes: Leaving the complex entries i and −i unchanged.
Changing 0 to some other value instead of leaving it as 0.
